import pydantic

from nova import api
from nova.types.pose import Pose


class RobotState(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """Collection of information on the current state of the robot.

    This class represents the complete state of a robot at a given point in time.

    Attributes:
        pose (Pose): The current pose (position and orientation) of the robot.
        tcp (str | None): The TCP name.
        joints (tuple[float, ...]): A tuple of joint angles in radians for each
            joint of the robot.
    """

    pose: Pose
    tcp: str | None
    joints: tuple[float, ...]


class MotionState(pydantic.BaseModel):
    """Collection of information on the current motion state of the robot"""

    motion_group_id: str
    path_parameter: float
    state: RobotState

"""Live integration tests for TrajectoryExecutor.

These require a running NOVA instance (``NOVA_API`` / ``NOVA_ACCESS_TOKEN``) and
are skipped unless the ``integration`` marker is selected. They use a *virtual*
controller, so no physical robot is moved.

The controller and the recorded trajectory are the example's own fixtures — the
only committed configuration with two motion groups on one controller, which is
what the IO barrier needs.
"""

import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import pytest_asyncio

from nova import Nova, api
from nova.actions import jnt
from nova.cell import MotionGroup, MultiMotionGroup

CONTROLLER = "kuka-executor-integration"
ROBOT, POSITIONER = f"0@{CONTROLLER}", f"1@{CONTROLLER}"
TCPS = {ROBOT: "1", POSITIONER: "0"}
SYNC_IO = "OUT#1"

# The barrier's promise is that no client round-trip sits between the starts, so
# the controllers acknowledge execution within the same state-publication tick.
# A start serialized over the network would take tens of milliseconds per group.
MAX_START_SKEW_SECONDS = 0.05

_EXAMPLES = Path(__file__).parents[3] / "examples"


def _recorded_trajectory() -> api.models.MultiJointTrajectory:
    """The example's trajectory, keyed for this test's controller."""
    stored = api.models.MultiJointTrajectory.model_validate_json(
        (_EXAMPLES / "multi_motion_group_trajectory.json").read_text()
    )
    samples = stored.joint_positions_by_motion_group_key
    return api.models.MultiJointTrajectory(
        joint_positions_by_motion_group_key={
            ROBOT: samples["0@kuka"],
            POSITIONER: samples["1@kuka"],
        },
        times=stored.times,
        locations=stored.locations,
    )


def _starts(trajectory: api.models.MultiJointTrajectory) -> dict[str, tuple[float, ...]]:
    samples = trajectory.joint_positions_by_motion_group_key
    return {name: tuple(samples[name][0]) for name in TCPS}


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope="module", loop_scope="module")
async def synchronized_groups():
    """Both motion groups of a virtual KUKA, standing at the recorded start.

    Getting there costs more than the tests themselves, so it is shared: the
    tests that do not need the recorded trajectory build theirs from wherever
    the groups stand. The robot is spawned at the start; ``initial_joint_position``
    places the first motion group only, so the positioner has to drive there.
    """
    starts = _starts(_recorded_trajectory())

    async with Nova() as nova:
        cell = nova.cell()
        await cell.ensure_controller(
            api.models.RobotController(
                name=CONTROLLER,
                configuration=api.models.VirtualController(
                    manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.KUKA,
                    type="kuka-kr210_r2700_2",
                    json=(_EXAMPLES / "multi_motion_group_controller.json").read_text(),
                    initial_joint_position=json.dumps([*starts[ROBOT], 0.0]),
                ),
            )
        )
        controller = await cell.controller(CONTROLLER)
        groups = {name: controller.motion_group(name) for name in TCPS}
        for name, group in groups.items():
            await group.plan_and_execute([jnt(list(starts[name]))], tcp=TCPS[name])
        yield controller, groups


async def _first_execution_acknowledgement(
    group, acknowledged: dict[str, object], name: str
) -> None:
    """Record when the controller reported this group's trajectory running."""
    async for state in group.stream_state():
        details = state.execute.details if state.execute else None
        if details is not None and isinstance(details.state, api.models.TrajectoryRunning):
            acknowledged[name] = state.timestamp
            return


async def _ramp_from_here(groups: dict[str, MotionGroup]) -> api.models.MultiJointTrajectory:
    """A two-second ramp of each group's last joint, starting where it stands.

    Taking the start from the live position keeps these tests independent of
    each other and of the recorded trajectory, which may only be executed from
    its own first sample.
    """
    samples, span, delta = 21, 2.0, 0.1
    parameter = [span * i / (samples - 1) for i in range(samples)]
    joints = {name: tuple(await group.joints()) for name, group in groups.items()}
    return api.models.MultiJointTrajectory(
        joint_positions_by_motion_group_key={
            name: [[*start[:-1], start[-1] + delta * p / span] for p in parameter]
            for name, start in joints.items()
        },
        times=parameter,
        locations=parameter,
    )


def _ensemble(groups: dict[str, MotionGroup]) -> MultiMotionGroup:
    return MultiMotionGroup.builder(groups).sync_on_io(SYNC_IO, controller=CONTROLLER).build()


@pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope="module")
@pytest.mark.integration
async def test_execute_recorded_trajectory_starts_both_groups_in_one_tick(synchronized_groups):
    """The barrier starts both groups together and runs the trajectory to its end."""
    controller, groups = synchronized_groups
    trajectory = _recorded_trajectory()
    samples = trajectory.joint_positions_by_motion_group_key

    acknowledged: dict[str, object] = {}
    watchers = [
        asyncio.create_task(_first_execution_acknowledgement(group, acknowledged, name))
        for name, group in groups.items()
    ]
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(_ensemble(groups).execute(trajectory, tcp=TCPS), timeout=120)
    finally:
        for watcher in watchers:
            watcher.cancel()

    for name, group in groups.items():
        expected = tuple(samples[name][-1])
        reached = tuple(await group.joints())
        assert max(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(reached, expected)) < 1e-3

    assert set(acknowledged) == set(groups)
    skew = abs((acknowledged[ROBOT] - acknowledged[POSITIONER]).total_seconds())
    assert skew <= MAX_START_SKEW_SECONDS
    assert await controller.read(SYNC_IO) is True


@pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope="module")
@pytest.mark.integration
async def test_forward_to_intermediate_target_keeps_the_session_open(synchronized_groups):
    """Stopping at an intermediate target must not end the session.

    The controller reports ``TrajectoryEnded`` at every commanded stop, so a
    session that trusted that state would tear down here instead of letting the
    caller step on.
    """
    _, groups = synchronized_groups
    trajectory = await _ramp_from_here(groups)

    async with _ensemble(groups).attach(trajectory, tcp=TCPS) as cursor:
        await asyncio.wait_for(cursor.forward_to(1.0), timeout=60)
        assert 1.0 - 0.01 <= cursor.current_location < 2.0

        # The session is still usable: stepping on reaches the end.
        await asyncio.wait_for(cursor.forward(), timeout=60)
        assert cursor.current_location >= 2.0 - 0.01


@pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope="module")
@pytest.mark.integration
async def test_pause_then_forward_rearms_the_barrier(synchronized_groups):
    """A paused session resumes through the barrier and reaches the end."""
    _, groups = synchronized_groups
    trajectory = await _ramp_from_here(groups)
    ends = {
        name: tuple(joints[-1])
        for name, joints in trajectory.joint_positions_by_motion_group_key.items()
    }

    async with _ensemble(groups).attach(trajectory, tcp=TCPS) as cursor:
        forward = cursor.forward()
        while cursor.current_location <= 0.0:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
        paused = cursor.pause()
        assert paused is not None
        await asyncio.wait_for(paused, timeout=30)
        with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
            await forward

        paused_at = cursor.current_location
        assert paused_at < 2.0

        await asyncio.wait_for(cursor.forward(), timeout=60)
        assert cursor.current_location > paused_at

1	"""Synchronized execution of one trajectory across multiple motion groups.
2	
3	Each motion group keeps its own :class:`TrajectoryCursor` and
4	``executeTrajectory`` websocket; the executor owns what spans them — task
5	supervision, the start barrier and the session monitors.
6	
7	Synchronization rests on one invariant, carried structurally by the trajectory
8	type: all groups of an :class:`api.models.MultiJointTrajectory` share a single
9	``times`` and a single ``locations`` array, so equal location means the same
10	instant on every path. The multi-motion-group RRT endpoint produces this type
11	directly; externally planned trajectories construct it explicitly.
12	
13	Movement starts run a barrier so the groups start on their controllers' own IO
14	image rather than on N network round-trips:
15	
16	1. the sync IO is cleared,
17	2. every cursor is armed with ``forward(start_on_io=...)``,
18	3. the executor waits until *every* group reports ``TrajectoryWaitForIO``
19	   (on a live, future-only subscription, so a stale state from an earlier
20	   start can never satisfy the barrier),
21	4. the sync IO is set.
22	
23	Example:
24	    ```python
25	    executor = (
26	        TrajectoryExecutor.builder({"0@robot": robot_mg, "0@positioner": positioner_mg})
27	        .sync_on_io("sync_out", controller="robot")
28	        .build()
29	    )
30	    await executor.execute(multi_joint_trajectory)
31	
32	    # Or interactively:
33	    async with executor.attach(multi_joint_trajectory) as cursor:
34	        operation = cursor.forward()
35	        cursor.pause()
36	        await cursor.forward()  # resumes through the barrier again
37	    ```
38	"""

41	import functools
42	from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
43	from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
44	from dataclasses import dataclass
45	from typing import Self

47	from nova import api
48	from nova.actions.io import WriteAction, io_write
49	from nova.cell.motion_group import MotionGroup
50	from nova.cell.movement_controller.trajectory_cursor import TrajectoryCursor
51	from nova.cell.multi_trajectory_cursor import IOSyncDriver, MultiTrajectoryCursor, SyncDriver
52	from nova.cell.session_monitor import SessionMonitor, SyncDriftMonitor

55	@dataclass(frozen=True)
56	class GroupArgs:
57	    """Per-group arguments for one execution.
58	
59	    Actions are not part of this: an action list belongs to one motion group's
60	    trajectory, whose integer locations are *its* action boundaries, and the
61	    ensemble has one shared parameterization instead. Synchronized execution
62	    therefore carries no action metadata and no IO overlay derived from it.
63	
64	    Attributes:
65	        tcp: TCP the trajectory was planned for; passed to trajectory loading.
66	        ignore_controller_limits: Skip the executing side's limit check when
67	            initializing the movement, on by default.
68	
69	            The executing side (RAE) rescales a trajectory it finds to be over
70	            the controller's limits — including trajectories that are within
71	            them, which is a defect on that side. Either way it rescales each
72	            motion group on its own, so the groups stop sharing one time
73	            parameterization and equal location no longer means the same
74	            instant: exactly the invariant synchronization rests on. The
75	            trajectory reaching the executor was planned against the same
76	            limits, so skipping the check costs nothing here and is the only
77	            way to keep it as planned. Turn it off for a group whose trajectory
78	            was not planned by Nova.
79	        state_stream_rate_msecs: Rate of this group's motion-group state
80	            stream, in milliseconds. None means the controller's own step
81	            rate — the fastest the server emits. The shared stream is opened
82	            at the rate of its first subscriber; see
83	            :meth:`MotionGroup.stream_state`.
84	        pause_on_io: This group's pause signal, attached to every start the
85	            group's cursor emits. The controller pauses the group on path while
86	            the condition holds; the others keep running. Resume is the
87	            caller's call (:meth:`MultiTrajectoryCursor.forward` once the
88	            signal cleared) — the controller does not resume by itself. The
89	            same condition may be given to several groups to pause them all.
90	    """
91	
92	    tcp: str | None = None
93	    ignore_controller_limits: bool = True
94	    state_stream_rate_msecs: int | None = None

98	class TrajectoryExecutor:
99	    """Long-lived owner of synchronized multi-motion-group execution.
100	
101	    Created once per topology — which motion groups, how they synchronize — and
102	    holds no per-run state; trajectories are per-call arguments and each run
103	    gets its own session (:meth:`attach` / :meth:`execute`).
104	
105	    Every execution goes through the barrier, so a single group with a
106	    hardware-gated start is a valid topology; plain single-group execution is
107	    :meth:`MotionGroup.execute`'s job. Groups need not share a cell or gateway
108	    — each is executed through its own — but a :class:`SyncDriver` may require
109	    it (:class:`IOSyncDriver` writes within one cell).
110	
111	    ``monitors`` observe every session's state streams; one that raises aborts
112	    the session.
113	    """
114	
115	    def __init__(
116	        self,
117	        motion_groups: Mapping[str, MotionGroup],
118	        sync: SyncDriver,
119	        monitors: Sequence[SessionMonitor] = (),
120	    ):
121	        if not motion_groups:
122	            raise ValueError("At least one motion group is required")
123	        groups_without_condition = set(motion_groups) - set(sync.start_conditions())
124	        if groups_without_condition:
125	            raise ValueError(
126	                f"The sync driver has no start condition for groups: "
127	                f"{sorted(groups_without_condition)}"
128	            )
129	
130	        self._motion_groups = dict(motion_groups)
131	        self._monitors = tuple(monitors)
132	        self._sync = sync
133	
134	    async def execute(
135	        self,
136	        trajectory: api.models.MultiJointTrajectory,
137	        groups: Mapping[str, GroupArgs] | None = None,
138	    ) -> None:
139	        """Execute the trajectory front to end, synchronized through the barrier."""
140	        async with self.attach(trajectory, groups) as cursor:
141	            await cursor.forward()

143	    @asynccontextmanager
144	    async def attach(
145	        self,
146	        trajectory: api.models.MultiJointTrajectory,
147	        groups: Mapping[str, GroupArgs] | None = None,
148	    ) -> AsyncGenerator[MultiTrajectoryCursor, None]:
149	        """Open a session for interactive control: load the trajectory, open the
150	        sockets, initialize — but do not move. Starting is the caller's call
151	        (:meth:`MultiTrajectoryCursor.forward`); exiting the context detaches
152	        every cursor and closes every socket."""
153	        per_group = self._split_for_groups(trajectory)
154	        unknown_group_args = set(groups or {}) - set(self._motion_groups)
155	        if unknown_group_args:
156	            raise ValueError(f"Group args given for unknown groups: {sorted(unknown_group_args)}")
157	
158	        cursors: dict[str, TrajectoryCursor] = {}
159	        for name, joint_trajectory in per_group.items():
160	            motion_group = self._motion_groups[name]
161	            group_args = (groups or {}).get(name) or GroupArgs()
162	            trajectory_id = await motion_group._load_planned_motion(
163	                joint_trajectory, group_args.tcp
164	            )
165	            # Binding the rate keeps the cursor's zero-arg stream factory seam
166	            # untouched; with no rate the bare bound method is passed, exactly
167	            # as before.
168	            state_stream_source = (
169	                functools.partial(motion_group.stream_state, group_args.state_stream_rate_msecs)
170	                if group_args.state_stream_rate_msecs is not None
171	                else motion_group.stream_state
172	            )
173	            cursors[name] = TrajectoryCursor(
174	                motion_id=trajectory_id,
175	                motion_group_state_stream=state_stream_source,
176	                joint_trajectory=joint_trajectory,
177	                detach_on_standstill=False,
178	                emit_motion_events=False,
179	                ignore_controller_limits=group_args.ignore_controller_limits,
180	                pause_on_io=group_args.pause_on_io,
181	            )
182	
183	        cursor = MultiTrajectoryCursor(cursors, self._sync)
184	        try:
185	            async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as task_group:
186	                # control() owns the barrier and the state fan-out in its own
187	                # TaskGroup; the executor only adds what needs its motion groups —
188	                # the executeTrajectory sockets — and the session monitors.
189	                for name in cursors:
190	                    task_group.create_task(
191	                        self._run_execute_trajectory(name, cursors[name]),
192	                        name=f"execute-trajectory-{name}",
193	                    )
194	                for monitor in self._monitors:
195	                    task_group.create_task(
196	                        monitor.run(cursor.monitor_streams()),
197	                        name=f"session-monitor-{type(monitor).__name__}",
198	                    )
199	                task_group.create_task(cursor.control(), name="multi-trajectory-cursor-control")
200	                try:
201	                    yield cursor
202	                finally:

204	                    for group_cursor in cursors.values():

206	        except BaseExceptionGroup as error_group:

208	            # TaskGroup wrapper — same unwrapping the cursor itself applies.
209	            if len(error_group.exceptions) == 1 and isinstance(
210	                error_group.exceptions[0], Exception
211	            ):

215	    def _split_for_groups(
216	        self, trajectory: api.models.MultiJointTrajectory
217	    ) -> dict[str, api.models.JointTrajectory]:
218	        """Split into per-group ``JointTrajectory`` for loading; every part
219	        carries the trajectory's single ``times``/``locations`` parameterization."""
220	        joint_positions_by_group = trajectory.joint_positions_by_motion_group_key
221	        if set(joint_positions_by_group) != set(self._motion_groups):
222	            raise ValueError(
223	                f"Trajectory keys {sorted(joint_positions_by_group)} must match the executor's "
224	                f"motion groups {sorted(self._motion_groups)}"
225	            )

227	            key: api.models.JointTrajectory(
228	                joint_positions=joint_samples,
229	                times=trajectory.times,
230	                locations=trajectory.locations,
231	            )
232	            for key, joint_samples in joint_positions_by_group.items()
233	        }

235	    async def _run_execute_trajectory(self, name: str, cursor: TrajectoryCursor) -> None:
236	        # Addressed through the group's own cell and gateway: executing does not
237	        # assume the groups share either, only the IO barrier does.
238	        motion_group = self._motion_groups[name]
239	        await motion_group._api_client.trajectory_execution_api.execute_trajectory(
240	            cell=motion_group._cell,
241	            controller=motion_group._controller_id,
242	            client_request_generator=cursor.cntrl,  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]

246	    def builder(
247	        cls, motion_groups: Mapping[str, MotionGroup] | Iterable[MotionGroup]
248	    ) -> "TrajectoryExecutorBuilder":
249	        """Start fluent assembly: ``TrajectoryExecutor.builder(...)...build()``.
250	
251	        ``motion_groups`` is either a mapping of names to motion groups, or
252	        just the motion groups — then their ids are the names.
253	        """

257	class TrajectoryExecutorBuilder:
258	    """Fluent assembly of a :class:`TrajectoryExecutor`.
259	
260	    The basic scenario is two calls — the motion groups and the sync IO:
261	
262	    ```python
263	    executor = (
264	        TrajectoryExecutor.builder([robot_mg, positioner_mg])
265	        .sync_on_io("sync_out", controller="robot")
266	        .build()
267	    )
268	    ```
269	
270	    :meth:`sync_on_io` states all three pieces of the barrier — the release
271	    write, the clear write and every group's start condition — so nothing is
272	    inferred later. :meth:`release_io`, :meth:`clear_io` and :meth:`watch`
273	    state the same pieces one at a time, for topologies where they are not one
274	    boolean IO; called after :meth:`sync_on_io` they replace what it set. A
275	    drift monitor runs by default — :meth:`monitors` replaces it. A custom
276	    :class:`SyncDriver` goes through the plain constructor instead.
277	    """
278	
279	    def __init__(self, motion_groups: Mapping[str, MotionGroup] | Iterable[MotionGroup]):
280	        self._motion_groups = (
281	            dict(motion_groups)
282	            if isinstance(motion_groups, Mapping)
283	            else {motion_group.id: motion_group for motion_group in motion_groups}
284	        )
285	        if not self._motion_groups:
286	            raise ValueError("At least one motion group is required")
287	        self._release: WriteAction | None = None
288	        self._clear: WriteAction | None = None
289	        self._watch: dict[str, api.models.StartOnIO] = {}
290	        self._monitors: tuple[SessionMonitor, ...] | None = None
291	
292	    def sync_on_io(
293	        self,
294	        io: str,
295	        controller: str | None = None,
296	        *,
297	        origin: api.models.IOOrigin = api.models.IOOrigin.CONTROLLER,
298	        release_value: bool = True,
299	    ) -> Self:
300	        """Synchronize on one boolean IO: releasing the barrier writes
301	        ``release_value`` to it, clearing writes the other value, and every
302	        group watches it for ``release_value``.
303	
304	        ``controller`` may be omitted when all motion groups share one; pass
305	        ``origin=IOOrigin.BUS_IO`` for a cell-wide bus variable.
306	        """
307	        self._release = self._write(io, release_value, controller, origin)
308	        self._clear = self._write(io, not release_value, controller, origin)
309	        condition = api.models.StartOnIO(
310	            io=api.models.IOBooleanValue(io=io, value=release_value),
311	            comparator=api.models.Comparator.COMPARATOR_EQUALS,
312	            io_origin=origin,
313	        )
314	        self._watch = {group: condition for group in self._motion_groups}
315	        return self
316	
317	    def release_io(
318	        self,
319	        io: str,
320	        value: bool,
321	        controller: str | None = None,
322	        *,
323	        origin: api.models.IOOrigin = api.models.IOOrigin.CONTROLLER,
324	    ) -> Self:
325	        """Release the barrier with this write — the counterpart of
326	        :meth:`clear_io` when the two are not one IO's two values."""
327	        self._release = self._write(io, value, controller, origin)
328	        return self
329	
330	    def clear_io(
331	        self,
332	        io: str,
333	        value: bool,
334	        controller: str | None = None,
335	        *,
336	        origin: api.models.IOOrigin = api.models.IOOrigin.CONTROLLER,
337	    ) -> Self:
338	        """Clear the barrier with this write — the counterpart of
339	        :meth:`release_io`."""
340	        self._clear = self._write(io, value, controller, origin)
341	        return self
342	
343	    def watch(self, group: str, condition: api.models.StartOnIO) -> Self:
344	        """Gate one group's start on this condition instead of on the release
345	        write itself (e.g. the wired input the sync IO physically lands on)."""
346	        if group not in self._motion_groups:
347	            raise ValueError(
348	                f"Unknown motion group '{group}'; known groups are {sorted(self._motion_groups)}"
349	            )
350	        self._watch[group] = condition
351	        return self
352	
353	    def monitors(self, *monitors: SessionMonitor) -> Self:
354	        """Replace the default session monitors (a :class:`SyncDriftMonitor`);
355	        call with no arguments to run without any."""
356	        self._monitors = monitors
357	        return self
358	
359	    def build(self) -> TrajectoryExecutor:
360	        if self._release is None:
361	            raise ValueError("The barrier has no release write: call sync_on_io() or release_io()")
362	        if self._clear is None:
363	            raise ValueError("The barrier has no clear write: call sync_on_io() or clear_io()")
364	        barrier_group = self._barrier_group()
365	        return TrajectoryExecutor(
366	            self._motion_groups,
367	            IOSyncDriver(
368	                clear=self._clear,
369	                release=self._release,
370	                watch=self._watch,
371	                api_client=barrier_group._api_client,
372	                cell=barrier_group._cell,
373	            ),
374	            self._monitors if self._monitors is not None else (SyncDriftMonitor(),),
375	        )
376	
377	    def _barrier_group(self) -> MotionGroup:
378	        """The motion group whose cell and gateway carry the IO barrier.
379	
380	        The IO barrier writes into a single cell — bus IO is cell-scoped, and a
381	        controller output is addressed as (cell, controller) — so groups spanning
382	        cells need a driver built for the cell that carries the sync IO.
383	        """
384	        cells = {motion_group._cell for motion_group in self._motion_groups.values()}
385	        if len(cells) > 1:
386	            raise ValueError(
387	                f"The IO barrier writes into one cell but the motion groups span {sorted(cells)}. "
388	                "Build an IOSyncDriver for the cell carrying the sync IO and pass it to "
389	                "TrajectoryExecutor directly."
390	            )
391	        return next(iter(self._motion_groups.values()))
392	
393	    def _write(
394	        self, io: str, value: bool, controller: str | None, origin: api.models.IOOrigin
395	    ) -> WriteAction:
396	        """Build a sync write, resolving its controller when it is unambiguous."""
397	        if origin is not api.models.IOOrigin.BUS_IO and controller is None:
398	            controllers = {
399	                motion_group._controller_id for motion_group in self._motion_groups.values()
400	            }
401	            if len(controllers) > 1:
402	                raise ValueError(
403	                    f"The controller for sync IO '{io}' is ambiguous: the motion groups span "
404	                    f"controllers {sorted(controllers)}. Pass the controller explicitly."
405	                )
406	            controller = next(iter(controllers))
407	        return io_write(io, value, device_id=controller, origin=origin)

content.text:
It's a real, deterministic failure — but it's not caused by this PR.

**What's failing:** `test_forward_to_intermediate_target_keeps_the_session_open` in `tests/nova/cell/test_trajectory_executor_integration.py`, every single retry (3/3 in this run, and 3/3 in the prior run on this same PR branch — 6/6 total). It always fails at the same line with `cursor.current_location` landing around 1.06–1.08 instead of the required `>= 1.99`, i.e. resuming after an intermediate stop only creeps forward a little instead of running to the end. That consistency (same assertion, same value range every time) rules out ordinary network/timing flakiness.

**Why it's not this PR's fault:** PR #520's diff only touches `motion_group.py` (`get_state`/`joints` → commanded joints), `motion_group_models.py` (adds robot model name literals), and `state.py` (adds `commanded_joints` field). None of that code is on the execution path this test exercises — `TrajectoryExecutor.attach()`/`TrajectoryCursor.forward()` never call `motion_group.joints()` or `get_state()`; they stream directly against the pre-loaded trajectory.

I confirmed this by checking CI on completely unrelated branches from the same day:
- `feat/upgrade-python-3.12` (a Python version bump, unrelated code) — same test, same failure, same ~1.07 value, on 3/3 retries.
- The last green run of this suite was `feat/path-triggers` on 2026-09-17 (before merge #509).
- Every branch that includes commit `51861139` (path-triggers, merged to main 2026-09-17) fails this exact test 100% of the time in every run I checked.

So something merged into `main` around the path-triggers merge (or a change on the live NOVA test instance CI provisions) broke "resume after an intermediate stop" for everyone, and it's now failing on any branch built on current main — independent of the commanded-joints change.

**Recommendation:** this isn't something to fix on `feature/Use-commanded-joints-as-start-joints`; it's a pre-existing regression on `main` that should be tracked/fixed separately. I'd flag it to whoever owns the path-triggers work rather than blocking this PR on it — happy to dig further into root cause on main if you want.
analyse it in a new branch from main in a separate worktree
I'll create a worktree branched from `origin/main` and switch into it for the investigation.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Description: Retrieve access token, create instance, create default cell,
4	             and verify that all services are up using NATS subscriptions.
5	"""
6	
7	import asyncio
8	import json
9	import os
10	import sys
11	from datetime import datetime
12	
13	import requests
14	from loguru import logger
15	
16	from nova import Nova
17	from nova.config import NovaConfig
18	
19	# TODO use env or command line args for these
20	CELL_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECS = 180.0
21	SERVICES_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECS = 180.0
22	
23	
24	async def wait_for_services_ready(nova: Nova, cell: str, timeout: float) -> None:
25	    """
26	    Wait for all services in a cell to be running using NATS subscription.
27	
28	    Args:
29	        nova: The Nova client instance.
30	        cell: The cell name to monitor.
31	        timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds.
32	    """
33	    cell_status_subject = f"nova.v2.cells.{cell}.status"
34	    all_services_ready = asyncio.Event()
35	
36	    async def on_cell_status_message(msg):
37	        if all_services_ready.is_set():
38	            return
39	        try:
40	            data = json.loads(msg.data)
41	            if not data:
42	                return
43	
44	            # Check if all services are running
45	            all_running = all(
46	                service.get("status", {}).get("code") == "Running" for service in data
47	            )
48	            if all_running:
49	                service_count = len(data)
50	                logger.info(f"✅ All {service_count} services in cell '{cell}' are running.")
51	                all_services_ready.set()
52	            else:
53	                not_running = [
54	                    f"{s['service']}: {s.get('status', {}).get('code')}"
55	                    for s in data
56	                    if s.get("status", {}).get("code") != "Running"
57	                ]
58	                logger.debug(f"Services not ready: {not_running}")
59	        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
60	            logger.warning(f"Failed to parse status message: {e}")
61	
62	    sub = await nova.nats.subscribe(subject=cell_status_subject, cb=on_cell_status_message)
63	    logger.info(f"Subscribed to {cell_status_subject}")
64	    try:
65	        await asyncio.wait_for(all_services_ready.wait(), timeout=timeout)
66	    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
67	        logger.error(f"Timeout waiting for services in cell '{cell}' to be ready")
68	        raise TimeoutError(f"Services not ready within {timeout}s")
69	    finally:
70	        await sub.unsubscribe()
71	
72	
73	async def main() -> None:
74	    refresh_url = os.getenv("PORTAL_PROD_REFRESH_URL")
75	    client_id = os.getenv("PORTAL_PROD_REFRESH_CLIENT_ID")
76	    refresh_token = os.getenv("PORTAL_PROD_REFRESH_TOKEN")
77	    if not refresh_url or not client_id or not refresh_token:
78	        logger.error(
79	            "[ERROR] Missing one of the required environment variables: "
80	            "PORTAL_PROD_REFRESH_URL, PORTAL_PROD_REFRESH_CLIENT_ID, PORTAL_PROD_REFRESH_TOKEN"
81	        )
82	        sys.exit(1)
83	
84	    get_token_response = requests.post(
85	        refresh_url,
86	        headers={"content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
87	        data={
88	            "grant_type": "refresh_token",
89	            "client_id": client_id,
90	            "refresh_token": refresh_token,
91	        },
92	    )
93	    get_token_response.raise_for_status()
94	    access_token = get_token_response.json().get("access_token")
95	
96	    github_run_id = os.getenv("GITHUB_RUN_ID", "local-run")
97	    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
98	    sandbox_name = f"svcmgr-{github_run_id}-{timestamp}"
99	
100	    response = requests.post(
101	        "https://api.portal.wandelbots.io/v1/instances",
102	        headers={
103	            "accept": "application/json",
104	            "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}",
105	            "Content-Type": "application/json",
106	        },
107	        json={"sandbox_name": sandbox_name},
108	    )
109	    response.raise_for_status()
110	    instance_response = response.json()
111	
112	    host = instance_response.get("host")
113	    instance_id = instance_response.get("instance_id")
114	
115	    config = NovaConfig(host=f"https://{host}", access_token=access_token)
116	    async with Nova(config) as nova:
117	        # Wait for cell to exist (API must be reachable for NATS connection)
118	        logger.info("Waiting for cell readiness (%fs)...", CELL_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECS)
119	        async with asyncio.timeout(CELL_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECS):
120	            while True:
121	                try:
122	                    cells = await nova.api.cell_api.list_cells()
123	                    if len(cells) > 0 and cells[0] == "cell":
124	                        logger.info("✅ Default cell 'cell' created.")
125	                        break
126	                except Exception as e:
127	                    logger.error(f"Waiting for default cell to be created: {e}")
128	                finally:
129	                    await asyncio.sleep(5)
130	
131	        # Wait for all services using NATS subscription
132	        logger.info(
133	            "Waiting for services readiness via NATS (%fs)...", SERVICES_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECS
134	        )
135	        await wait_for_services_ready(nova, "cell", SERVICES_READINESS_TIMEOUT_SECS)
136	
137	    with open("instance_config.env", "w") as file:
138	        file.write(
139	            f"""
140	PORTAL_PROD_ACCESS_TOKEN="{access_token}"
141	PORTAL_PROD_HOST="{host}"
142	PORTAL_PROD_INSTANCE_ID="{instance_id}"
143	"""
144	        )
145	
146	
147	if __name__ == "__main__":
148	    asyncio.run(main())

1	# Trajectory Execution State Machine
2	
3	This module provides `TrajectoryExecutionMachine`, a finite-state machine that encapsulates the state handling logic for trajectory execution lifecycle, shared across movement controllers (`move_forward`, `TrajectoryCursor`, etc.).
4	
5	## How the controller publishes execution state
6	
7	Execution progress is **observed** on the `MotionGroupState` stream — the `executeTrajectory`
8	websocket only acknowledges requests and never delivers a completion message. The
9	`execute.details.state` discriminator (`RUNNING`, `END_OF_TRAJECTORY`, `PAUSED_BY_USER`,
10	`WAIT_FOR_IO`, `PAUSED_ON_IO`) together with the top-level `standstill` flag is the entire signal.
11	
12	RAE publishes the execute state **level-based** (robotics/wbr!2262):
13	
14	- The `execute` block is present from `InitializeMovementRequest` until the execution is stopped
15	  or its websocket is torn down — its mere presence does **not** mean the robot is moving.
16	- Terminal and paused states are **re-published every controller step** while they hold:
17	  `END_OF_TRAJECTORY` after the motion ends, `PAUSED_BY_USER` for as long as a pause holds.
18	  Completion and pause are durable, re-observable conditions — no consumer has to catch a
19	  single-step event, so any state-stream rate detects them.
20	- Between `InitializeMovementRequest` and the actual motion start the state is also
21	  `PAUSED_BY_USER` (at standstill): a *parked* trajectory is indistinguishable from a paused one
22	  on the wire. Consumers must not conclude a movement operation from a paused state unless that
23	  operation was actually seen running (see the cursor rules below).
24	- A stopped execution also reports `PAUSED_BY_USER` (there is no separate wire kind); after
25	  stop/teardown the `execute` block disappears.
26	
27	Controllers **older than wbr!2262** instead drop the `execute` block the instant the robot
28	settles: `END_OF_TRAJECTORY` / `PAUSED_BY_USER` are visible at standstill for only one or two
29	control cycles, after which nothing but bare standstill frames arrive. Since every stream between
30	the control loop and a client may drop frames, the machine treats a bare standstill frame as the
31	completion of an already-observed `ending`/`pausing` — the discriminator was seen on the way in,
32	the standstill concludes it.
33	
34	## States
35	
36	| State | Description |
37	|-------|-------------|
38	| `idle` | Initial state — no trajectory active, waiting for `start` |
39	| `executing` | Robot is moving (`TrajectoryRunning`) |
40	| `ending` | `TrajectoryEnded` received but robot not yet at standstill |
41	| `pausing` | `TrajectoryPausedByUser` received, not yet at standstill |
42	| `paused` | Robot paused and at standstill — may `start` again to resume |
43	| `ended` | Trajectory finished **and** robot at standstill |
44	| `error` | Unrecoverable error — terminal state |
45	
46	## Transitions
47	
48	### External Commands
49	- `start` — begin or resume execution (from `idle`, `paused`, or `ended`)
50	- `fail` — signal an error from any non-terminal state
51	
52	### Internal Transitions (via `process_motion_state`)
53	- `TrajectoryRunning` → stay in `executing`
54	- `TrajectoryEnded` + standstill → `ended`
55	- `TrajectoryEnded` (no standstill) → `ending` → (on standstill) → `ended`
56	- `TrajectoryPausedByUser` + standstill → `paused`
57	- `TrajectoryPausedByUser` (no standstill) → `pausing` → (on standstill) → `paused`
58	
59	The standstill that completes `ending → ended` and `pausing → paused` counts **with or without an
60	`execute` block on the frame**: pre-!2262 controllers drop the block at settle, so a bare
61	standstill frame can be the only completion signal that ever arrives. A bare standstill never
62	concludes anything from `executing` — without a terminal discriminator there is nothing to
63	conclude.
64	
65	## Completion rules in `TrajectoryCursor`
66	
67	The cursor derives *operation* completion from the machine, with two guards for level-based
68	publishing:
69	
70	- `pause()` always queues a pause command while the cursor is attached, even when the local
71	  operation has already completed. Local operation state cannot prove that the controller has
72	  stopped, so it must not suppress a stop request. The returned future reports completion or a
73	  controller error; calling `pause()` after detaching returns a failed future.
74	- An operation is only marked running on **evidence of motion** (`standstill` false or a
75	  `RUNNING` detail) — never on the mere presence of an `execute` block, which exists from
76	  initialization on.
77	- A `paused` machine state concludes only a PAUSE operation, or a movement operation that was
78	  seen running. This keeps the persistent pre-start `PAUSED_BY_USER` frames from resolving a
79	  movement that never moved.
80	- `ended` concludes any commanded operation; in one-shot mode (`move_forward`) it also detaches
81	  the cursor, which closes the execution websocket — the client's teardown acknowledges the
82	  persistent terminal state.
83	
84	---

Analysis done (worktree `worktree-fix+intermediate-stop-resume`, branched from `origin/main` at `c7745998`). One correction to my earlier message: the path-triggers merge is **not** the culprit — the last green run already included it.

## What breaks

`test_forward_to_intermediate_target_keeps_the_session_open`: after `forward_to(1.0)` stops both groups at 1.0, the resume `forward()` sends a `StartMovementRequest` with **no** `target_location` (i.e. "run to the end", per the API docs). The controller then runs ~0.06 location units and reports `END_OF_TRAJECTORY` at 1.056–1.076 — in every one of the 12 attempts I checked across 4 runs. The cursor correctly completes the operation on that `ended` state, so `forward()` resolves at ~1.06 and the assertion `>= 1.99` fails.

The captured log confirms the sequence: per resume, ~30 parked `PAUSED_BY_USER`+standstill frames (harmless `start → _pause_immediately` cycling in the state machine), then `WAIT_FOR_IO`, then `RUNNING`, then `_end_immediately` / `_begin_ending → _end_after_standstill` — a real controller stop, not a mis-detected pause.

## Why it is the server, not the SDK

| Run | When (UTC) | main commit | api-client | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 35222878394 release-please | 09-17 12:44 | `51861139` | 26.7.0.dev24 | green (75 passed) |
| 35322738024 chore/extract-sbom | 09-18 08:06 | `51861139` (+ one script) | 26.7.0.dev24 | **fails**, 1.064 / 1.058 / 1.056 |
| 35328535865 feat/upgrade-python-3.12 | 09-18 09:14 | `693ffb9a` | 26.7.0 | fails, 1.076 / 1.074 / 1.076 |
| 35346320613 PR #520 | 09-18 12:44 | `c7745998` | 26.7.0 | fails, 1.066 / 1.07 / 1.06 |

Row 2 is decisive: identical SDK code (the branch only adds `scripts/extract_sbom_information.py`), identical lockfile and api-client, identical test — only the NOVA instance differs. `scripts/create_nova_instance.py` provisions a fresh portal sandbox per run, so every run gets whatever server build the portal currently ships. Something changed there between 09-17 14:45 and 09-18 10:00 CEST. Best hypothesis: the new controller build keeps the previous start's `target_location` (1.0) when a subsequent start carries none, so the resume "ends" right after passing it.

## Proposed SDK mitigation (not implemented yet)

In `TrajectoryCursor.forward()` / `backward()` (`nova/cell/movement_controller/trajectory_cursor.py:823/871`), send an explicit `target_location` when the caller gives none — `self.end_location` forward, `0.0` backward — when `joint_trajectory` is known (all production constructions pass it: `move_forward.py:26`, `tuner.py:157`, `trajectory_executor.py:176`). Per the API docs "target location takes precedence", so this is semantically identical on a correct server and immune to the retained-target behaviour. One existing unit test (`tests/cell/test_trajectory_executor.py:316`) asserts on intent target and would need a look.

Caveat: I could not reproduce live — no artifacts were uploaded by the failing runs and your local instance (172.31.10.67) isn't reachable from here — so the fix would be validated by CI on a fresh instance. Independently, the server regression should go to the RAE team; a sibling `test_pause_then_forward_rearms_the_barrier` only asserts `> paused_at`, so it would not catch the same truncation after a pause.

Want me to implement the mitigation + a unit test in this worktree and open a PR to let CI validate it?

"""Reproduce forward_to(1.0) then forward() on the executor and dump the raw wire frames."""

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from nova import Nova, api
from nova.actions import jnt
from nova.cell import MultiMotionGroup

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)

CONTROLLER = "kuka-executor-integration"
ROBOT, POSITIONER = f"0@{CONTROLLER}", f"1@{CONTROLLER}"
TCPS = {ROBOT: "1", POSITIONER: "0"}
SYNC_IO = "OUT#1"
EXAMPLES = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "examples"


def recorded():
    stored = api.models.MultiJointTrajectory.model_validate_json(
        (EXAMPLES / "multi_motion_group_trajectory.json").read_text()
    )
    s = stored.joint_positions_by_motion_group_key
    return {ROBOT: tuple(s["0@kuka"][0]), POSITIONER: tuple(s["1@kuka"][0])}


async def ramp(groups):
    samples, span, delta = 21, 2.0, 0.1
    p = [span * i / (samples - 1) for i in range(samples)]
    joints = {n: tuple(await g.joints()) for n, g in groups.items()}
    return api.models.MultiJointTrajectory(
        joint_positions_by_motion_group_key={
            n: [[*st[:-1], st[-1] + delta * q / span] for q in p] for n, st in joints.items()
        },
        times=p,
        locations=p,
    )


async def tap(name, stream, log, stop):
    last = None
    async for st in stream:
        if stop.is_set():
            return
        ex = st.execute
        det = ex.details if ex else None
        key = (
            type(det.state).__name__ if det is not None else None,
            round(det.location, 3) if det is not None else None,
            st.standstill,
        )
        if key != last:
            log.append((asyncio.get_running_loop().time(), name, *key))
            last = key


async def main():
    starts = recorded()
    async with Nova() as nova:
        cell = nova.cell()
        await cell.ensure_controller(
            api.models.RobotController(
                name=CONTROLLER,
                configuration=api.models.VirtualController(
                    manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.KUKA,
                    type="kuka-kr210_r2700_2",
                    json=(EXAMPLES / "multi_motion_group_controller.json").read_text(),
                    initial_joint_position=json.dumps([*starts[ROBOT], 0.0]),
                ),
            )
        )
        controller = await cell.controller(CONTROLLER)
        groups = {n: controller.motion_group(n) for n in TCPS}
        for n, g in groups.items():
            await g.plan_and_execute([jnt(list(starts[n]))], tcp=TCPS[n])

        trajectory = await ramp(groups)
        ensemble = MultiMotionGroup.builder(groups).sync_on_io(SYNC_IO, controller=CONTROLLER).build()

        log: list = []
        stop = asyncio.Event()
        taps = [asyncio.create_task(tap(n, g.stream_state(), log, stop)) for n, g in groups.items()]
        t0 = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
        async with ensemble.attach(trajectory, tcp=TCPS) as cursor:
            log.append((asyncio.get_running_loop().time(), "--", "forward_to(1.0)", None, None))
            r1 = await asyncio.wait_for(cursor.forward_to(1.0), timeout=60)
            log.append((asyncio.get_running_loop().time(), "--", f"forward_to done loc={cursor.current_location}", None, None))
            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
            log.append((asyncio.get_running_loop().time(), "--", "forward()", None, None))
            r2 = await asyncio.wait_for(cursor.forward(), timeout=60)
            log.append((asyncio.get_running_loop().time(), "--", f"forward done loc={cursor.current_location}", None, None))
            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
        stop.set()
        for t in taps:
            t.cancel()
        for row in log:
            t, name, *rest = row
            print(f"{t - t0:8.3f}  {name:28s} {rest}")
        print("results forward_to:", {k: (v.final_location, v.target_location) for k, v in r1.items()})
        print("results forward   :", {k: (v.final_location, v.target_location) for k, v in r2.items()})


asyncio.run(main())

1	"""Tests for the TrajectoryExecutionMachine state machine.
2	
3	These tests verify the state machine models the trajectory execution lifecycle
4	correctly, including forward/backward movement, pauses, standstill detection
5	and multi-phase completion (TrajectoryEnded followed by standstill).
6	"""
7	
8	import json
9	from datetime import datetime, timezone
10	from pathlib import Path
11	
12	import pytest
13	
14	from nova import api
15	from nova.cell.movement_controller.trajectory_state_machine import TrajectoryExecutionMachine
16	
17	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
18	# Helpers
19	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
20	
21	
22	def _make_motion_group_state(
23	    standstill: bool, execute: api.models.Execute | None = None
24	) -> api.models.MotionGroupState:
25	    """Create a MotionGroupState with the given standstill and execute fields."""
26	    return api.models.MotionGroupState(
27	        timestamp=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
28	        sequence_number=1,
29	        description_revision=0,
30	        motion_group="mg-0",
31	        controller="ctrl-0",
32	        joint_position=[0.0] * 6,
33	        joint_limit_reached=api.models.MotionGroupStateJointLimitReached(limit_reached=[False] * 6),
34	        standstill=standstill,
35	        execute=execute,
36	    )
37	
38	
39	def _make_execute(
40	    trajectory_state: (
41	        api.models.TrajectoryRunning
42	        | api.models.TrajectoryEnded
43	        | api.models.TrajectoryPausedByUser
44	    ),
45	    location: float = 1.0,
46	) -> api.models.Execute:
47	    """Create an Execute with TrajectoryDetails."""
48	    return api.models.Execute(
49	        joint_position=[0.0] * 6,
50	        details=api.models.TrajectoryDetails(
51	            trajectory="traj-123", location=location, state=trajectory_state
52	        ),
53	    )
54	
55	
56	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	# State machine lifecycle tests
58	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	
60	
61	class TestStateMachineLifecycle:
62	    """Basic lifecycle: idle → start → executing → completed."""
63	
64	    def test_initial_state_is_idle(self):
65	        machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
66	        assert machine.is_idle
67	
68	    def test_start_transitions_to_executing(self):
69	        machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
70	        machine.send("start")
71	        assert machine.is_executing
72	
73	    def test_ended_is_terminal(self):
74	        machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
75	        machine.send("start")
76	        state = _make_motion_group_state(
77	            standstill=True, execute=_make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryEnded())
78	        )
79	        machine.process_motion_state(state)
80	        assert machine.is_ended
81	        assert machine.is_terminal
82	
83	    def test_error_is_terminal(self):

def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.location: float | None = None
        # (state kind, location) of the last terminal frame seen, and the one a
        # resume must ignore while the controller still re-publishes it.
        self._last_terminal: tuple[type, float] | None = None
        self._stale_terminal: tuple[type, float] | None = None
        super().__init__()

    def on_start(self, source: State) -> None:
        # Level-based publishing (robotics/wbr!2262) keeps re-publishing the
        # terminal state of the previous stop until the controller has taken up
        # the new command. Resuming from `ended`/`paused` therefore first sees
        # the old END_OF_TRAJECTORY / PAUSED_BY_USER frames again; concluding
        # the new operation from them would report it finished at its start.
        # They are told apart from a genuine new terminal state by identity:
        # same kind at the same location as the state we are leaving. A genuine
        # one is always preceded by a different frame (WAIT_FOR_IO or RUNNING),
        # which lifts the filter.
        self._stale_terminal = self._last_terminal if source in (self.ended, self.paused) else None

class TestStaleTerminalFramesAfterResume:
    """Level-based publishing (robotics/wbr!2262) keeps re-publishing the
    previous stop's terminal state until the controller takes up the new
    command. A ``start`` out of ``ended``/``paused`` must not conclude from
    those frames — the virtual controller reproduced ``forward_to(1.0)`` then
    ``forward()`` resolving at 1.0 while the robot ran on to the end."""

    @staticmethod
    def _ended_at(machine: TrajectoryExecutionMachine, location: float) -> None:
        machine.send("start")
        machine.process_motion_state(
            _make_motion_group_state(
                standstill=True, execute=_make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryEnded(), location)
            )
        )
        assert machine.is_ended

    def test_re_published_end_of_previous_stop_is_ignored_after_start(self):
        machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
        self._ended_at(machine, 1.0)

        machine.send("start")
        for _ in range(3):
            result = machine.process_motion_state(
                _make_motion_group_state(
                    standstill=True, execute=_make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryEnded(), 1.0)
                )
            )
            assert machine.is_executing
            assert not result.state_changed
            assert result.location == 1.0

    def test_different_frame_lifts_the_filter_and_the_new_end_completes(self):
        machine = TrajectoryExecutionMachine()
        self._ended_at(machine, 1.0)
        machine.send("start")
        machine.process_motion_state(
            _make_motion_group_state(
                standstill=True, execute=_make_execute(api.models.TrajectoryEnded(), 1.0)
            )
        )

        machine.process_motion_state(
            _make_motion_group_state(

async def test_stepping_on_after_forward_to_is_not_resolved_by_the_re_published_end():
    """``forward_to(1.0)`` then ``forward()`` on one attached cursor — the
    executor's interactive flow, as reproduced on the virtual controller: after
    the stop at 1.0 the controller re-publishes END_OF_TRAJECTORY@1.0 every step
    until it takes up the new start, then WAIT_FOR_IO / RUNNING, then the real
    end. The second operation must resolve at 2.0, not at its own start."""
    frames: asyncio.Queue[api.models.MotionGroupState] = asyncio.Queue()
    cursor = TrajectoryCursor(
        motion_id="traj-1",
        motion_group_state_stream=_stream_from_queue(frames),
        joint_trajectory=_joint_trajectory(),
        initial_location=0.0,
        detach_on_standstill=False,
        emit_motion_events=False,
    )
    consumer = await _drive(cursor)

    async def feed(*states: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> None:
        for state in states:
            frames.put_nowait(state)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)

    try:
        first = cursor.forward_to(1.0)
        await feed(_state(False, _running(0.5)), _state(False, _ended(1.0)), _state(True, _ended(1.0)))
        async with asyncio.timeout(5):
            assert (await first).final_location == 1.0

        second = cursor.forward()
        # the previous stop, re-published while the command is on its way
        await feed(_state(True, _ended(1.0)), _state(True, _ended(1.0)), _state(True, _ended(1.0)))
        assert not second.done(), "the re-published end of the previous stop resolved the resume"

        await feed(
            _state(True, _waiting_for_io(1.0)),
            _state(True, _running(1.0)),
            _state(False, _running(1.5)),
            _state(True, _ended(2.0)),
            _state(True, _ended(2.0)),
        )
        async with asyncio.timeout(5):
            result = await second
        assert result.error is None
        assert result.final_location == 2.0
    finally:
        cursor.detach()
        async with asyncio.timeout(5):
            await asyncio.gather(consumer, return_exceptions=True)

`tests/nova/cell/test_trajectory_executor_integration.py::test_forward_to_intermediate_target_keeps_the_session_open`
failed deterministically on every branch from 2026-09-18 ~08:00 UTC: after `forward_to(1.0)` the resume

`ended` completion had no stale guard (only `paused` had `may_complete_as_paused`), so the resumed

content.text:
Reproduced, root-caused and fixed — all verified against 172.31.13.138.

## What actually happens (wire frames from the probe)

```
1.386  Ended @1.000  standstill=False      ← forward_to(1.0) reaches its target
1.390  Ended @1.000  standstill=True       → forward_to resolves, final=1.0
       … Ended @1.000 re-published every step for the next second …
2.390  forward()
2.430  WaitForIO @1.000                    ← controller has taken up the new start
2.458  Running @1.000 … 1.9 … 2.0          ← robot runs to the end
2.468  forward() resolves — final_location=1.0
```

The new server build publishes execute state **level-based** (wbr!2262): after the stop at 1.0 it keeps re-publishing `TrajectoryEnded@1.0` until it takes up the next command. The cursor's state machine, sent `start` for the resume, saw those stale END frames, went straight to `ended`, and completed the new operation at its own start location. The `paused` path already had a guard for exactly this (`may_complete_as_paused`); the `ended` path had none. So it's an SDK gap that the old server (which dropped the `execute` block at settle) never exposed — my earlier "server retains the target" hypothesis was wrong; the robot does run to the end, the SDK just stops watching.

A second live probe settled the design: a `forward()` issued *at* the end yields `WaitForIO@2.0 → Ended@2.0` with no `Running` frame, so a plain "seen running" guard would hang there.

## The fix (`nova/cell/movement_controller/trajectory_state_machine.py`, +48 lines)

`on_start` records the terminal state a `start` leaves from `ended`/`paused` (kind + location); `process_motion_state` ignores frames repeating exactly that until any different frame arrives (`WaitForIO`, `Running`, or a terminal state elsewhere), which lifts the filter. No change to the cursor or the monitor loop; README documents the rule.

## Verification

- Live, with fix: `test_trajectory_executor_integration.py` 3/3 pass (the failing test included); single-cursor, pause-on-io and movement integration files 10/10 pass.
- Unit: full suite 1016 passed; 7 new tests — 6 machine-level (stale END ignored, filter lifts on WaitForIO/Running, start-at-end case, stale PAUSED twin, no filter from idle) and one cursor-level replay of the exact `forward_to(1.0) → forward()` frame sequence.
- ruff format/check and ty clean.

Changed files (uncommitted, in the worktree on `worktree-fix+intermediate-stop-resume`): `trajectory_state_machine.py`, `README.md`, `tests/cell/test_trajectory_state_machine.py`, `tests/cell/test_trajectory_cursor_level_states.py`. The worktree `.env` (gitignored) points at your instance.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/q/0code/nova-python-sdk/.claude/skills/pr

# Open / update a pull request

This folder is the whole skill — enough to open a PR in any repo. Do not require
the repo's `AGENTS.md` to operate. If you already know repo extras
(ticket-as-scope, extra body sections, branch pattern, a PR template), apply them
**on top** of this skill — never instead of Why and Benefits.

Read [references/description.md](references/description.md) before writing title
or body.

Drive GitHub through the local authenticated `gh` CLI. Prefix `gh` with
`GH_PAGER=cat`. Never merge. Never force-push unless the user asked. Always end
the reply with the PR URL on its own last line.

## When to open (and when not to)

Only run this skill when the user asked to open, create, update, or refresh a PR.

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| User did **not** ask to open or update a PR | Do nothing. Do not create "while you're here". |
| Default branch, clean tree, no unique commits | Stop. Do not open an empty PR. |
| Default branch, has work to ship | **Always** create a new branch first (step 1). Never commit or push on the default branch. |
| Feature branch, unique commits, **no** PR for this head | Push (if needed) and **create** one PR (step 3). |
| Feature branch, a PR **already exists for this head** | **Update** that PR (step 4). Never `gh pr create`. |
| `gh pr view` / list shows a PR whose `headRefName` ≠ current branch | Stop. Do not edit the wrong PR. |
| Work is unfinished / user said WIP | Open or convert to **draft**. Title may use a `[WIP]` prefix. |
| Diff contains secrets, credentials, or `.env` files | Stop and tell the user. Do not open. |
| Two unrelated problems on the same branch | Flag the mixed scope. Do not silently describe them as one change. Do not split the branch unless asked. |

One head → one PR. Updating means **rewriting** title and body for the whole
branch, not appending "also…".

## 0. Context (always, in parallel)

```bash
git status -sb
git branch --show-current
git log --oneline -8
git diff && git diff --cached
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u} 2>/dev/null || true
GH_PAGER=cat gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq '.defaultBranchRef.name'
command -v gh && GH_PAGER=cat gh auth status
```

Default branch: the `gh` value, else `main`, else `master`.

If `gh` is missing or unauthenticated: still author title + body to a temp file,
then give the user the exact `git push` and `gh pr create --body-file` commands.
Do not invent a web-API fallback.

Decide:

- `type`: `feat` | `fix` | `docs` | `chore` | `refactor` | `perf` | `test` |
  `build` | `ci` (or another [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
  type that fits). Use `!` for a breaking change.
- `scope`: a ticket id if the user, branch, or commits have one (`ABC-123`);
  otherwise the area the diff belongs to. Omit `(scope)` when none is honest.
- `summary`: short imperative phrase (the what, not the why).

Title, under 72 characters:

```text
<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>
```

If the branch already has a conventional subject that still describes the
**whole** branch, reuse it. Do not title the PR after the last commit alone.

## 1. Branch

### On the default branch

Create a new branch before any commit, push, or `gh pr`:

```bash
git checkout -b <type>/<scope>-<slug>
```

If the repo documents a branch pattern, use that instead. `<slug>` is 2–4
lowercase words from the change. Uncommitted work comes along.

If the work is not yet committed and the user asked for a PR, commit it on the
**new** branch (conventional subject; body = why). Commit only files that belong
to this change; ask if the dirty tree is mixed.

### Already on a feature branch

Stay on it. Do not fork another branch. Do not create a second PR.

## 2. Existing PR?

```bash

## Summary
- Make `TrajectoryExecutionMachine` ignore frames that merely repeat the terminal state a `start` leaves (same kind at the same location) until the controller shows any different frame.
- Pin the behaviour with machine-level tests and a cursor-level replay of the observed frame sequence; document the rule in the movement-controller README.

## Why
Since 2026-09-18 every branch's integration CI failed `test_forward_to_intermediate_target_keeps_the_session_open`: after `forward_to(1.0)`, the follow-up `forward()` resolved at ~1.0 while the robot ran on to 2.0. The portal now provisions a controller build that publishes execute state level-based (robotics/wbr!2262): after the stop at 1.0 it re-publishes `END_OF_TRAJECTORY@1.0` every step until it takes up the next start (then `WAIT_FOR_IO → RUNNING → END@2.0`). The cursor sent `start` for the resume, saw those stale END frames first and concluded the new operation at its own start location. The `paused` path already guarded against this (`may_complete_as_paused`); the `ended` path did not. Not caused by any PR — reproduced with the SDK code and api-client of the last green run.

## Benefits
- Stepping on after an intermediate target, and every resume from `ended`/`paused`, reports the real stop again — the executor session and `MultiTrajectoryCursor` stay usable on current controllers.
- No behaviour change on controllers that drop the `execute` block at settle; nothing changes for a first start from `idle`.

## How
`on_start` records the (kind, location) of the terminal frame being left; `process_motion_state` treats frames matching it as `_keep_executing` until a different frame arrives, which lifts the filter. Identity by kind and location rather than a "seen RUNNING" guard is deliberate: a `forward()` issued at the very end answers `WAIT_FOR_IO@2.0` then `END@2.0` with no RUNNING frame in between (probed live), and a running guard would hang there.

## Test plan
- [x] Live on a fresh NOVA instance (172.31.13.138): `PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -m integration tests/nova/cell/test_trajectory_executor_integration.py` — 3 passed (fails 1.002 ≥ 1.99 without the fix)
- [x] Live: `tests/nova/cell/motion_group/test_trajectory_cursor_integration.py`, `test_pause_on_io.py`, `test_motion_group_movement.py` — 10 passed
- [x] Live probe of raw `stream_state()` frames around the resume and around a `forward()` issued at the end (WAIT_FOR_IO then END again, no RUNNING)
- [x] `PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -m "not integration"` — 1016 passed; 7 new tests (stale END/PAUSED ignored, filter lifts on WAIT_FOR_IO/RUNNING, start at the end, no filter from idle, cursor-level `forward_to(1.0)` then `forward()` replay)

1959cd66 feat(cell): resume controller-side IO pauses instead of ending the execution

A StartMovementRequest.pause_on_io condition makes the controller pause the
robot on path and report PAUSED_ON_IO (level-based). The SDK handled that state
like END_OF_TRAJECTORY, so execute()/plan_and_execute() returned mid-trajectory
the moment the signal was set and nothing could resume the motion.

Measured on NOVA 26.7.0 (see ADR 002): the controller never resumes by itself; a
new start on the same websocket resumes within ~100 ms once the condition cleared
and re-arms the pause; the ramp equals a PauseMovementRequest. The pause is per
motion group, controller and bus IOs alike.

- state machine: TrajectoryPausedOnIO -> pausing/paused with pause_reason; a
  RUNNING frame while paused is an observed resume
- cursor: an IO pause completes the movement operation with paused_on_io=True and
  keeps the cursor attached; frames re-publishing the terminal state an operation
  was started out of (PAUSED_ON_IO, or END after an intermediate forward_to) no

149	    """
150	    plan_and_execute(pause_on_io=...) must block through a controller-side IO pause:
151	
152	    - once moving, setting the IO pauses the robot on path (PAUSED_ON_IO)
153	    - execute() does not return while the signal holds (ADR 002)
154	    - clearing the IO resumes the motion; execute() returns at the target
155	    """
156	    initial_joint_positions = [0.0, -pi / 2, -pi / 2, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
157	    controller_name = "kuka-pause-behavior-test"
158	
159	    async with Nova() as nova:
160	        cell = nova.cell()
161	        await cell.ensure_controller(
162	            virtual_controller(
163	                name=controller_name,
164	                manufacturer=api.models.Manufacturer.KUKA,
165	                type="kuka-kr6_r700_sixx",
166	                position=initial_joint_positions,
167	            )
168	        )
169	
170	        kuka = await cell.controller(controller_name)
171	
172	        async with kuka[0] as mg:
173	            await kuka.write("OUT#900", False)
174	            # The run traverses the full 1.5 rad; start from home so repeated runs on
175	            # the shared virtual controller stay inside the joint limits.
176	            await mg.plan_and_execute([jnt(initial_joint_positions[:6])], tcp="Flange")
177	
178	            current_joints = await mg.joints()
179	            target_joints = list(current_joints)
180	            target_joints[0] += 1.5
181	
182	            pause_io = api.models.PauseOnIO(
183	                io=api.models.IOBooleanValue(io="OUT#900", value=True),
184	                comparator=api.models.Comparator.COMPARATOR_EQUALS,
185	                io_origin=api.models.IOOrigin.CONTROLLER,
186	            )
187	            actions = [jnt(target_joints, settings=MotionSettings(tcp_velocity_limit=30))]
188	
189	            async def wait_for_trajectory_state(kind: type, *, standstill: bool | None = None):
190	                # Observe the pause on the state stream instead of polling joints —
191	                # the level-based PAUSED_ON_IO is re-published every step.
192	                async for state in mg.stream_state(None):
193	                    details = state.execute.details if state.execute else None
194	                    if isinstance(details, api.models.TrajectoryDetails) and isinstance(
195	                        details.state, kind
196	                    ):
197	                        if standstill is None or state.standstill == standstill:
198	                            return state
199	
200	            motion_task = asyncio.create_task(
201	                mg.plan_and_execute(actions=actions, tcp="Flange", pause_on_io=pause_io)
202	            )
203	
204	            async def observe(kind: type, *, standstill: bool, timeout: float):
205	                """Wait for a trajectory state, surfacing a failed execute() instead of
206	                timing out on a state that will never come."""
207	                waiter = asyncio.ensure_future(
208	                    wait_for_trajectory_state(kind, standstill=standstill)
209	                )
210	                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(
211	                    {waiter, motion_task}, timeout=timeout, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
212	                )
213	                if waiter not in done:
214	                    waiter.cancel()
215	                    if motion_task in done:
216	                        motion_task.result()  # raises the execute() error
217	                    raise TimeoutError(
218	                        f"no {kind.__name__} (standstill={standstill}) in {timeout}s"
219	                    )
220	                return waiter.result()
221	
222	            try:
223	                await observe(api.models.TrajectoryRunning, standstill=False, timeout=20.0)
224	                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
225	                await kuka.write("OUT#900", True)
226	
227	                paused = await observe(
228	                    api.models.TrajectoryPausedOnIO, standstill=True, timeout=10.0
229	                )
230	                paused_joints = list(paused.joint_position)
231	                assert abs(paused_joints[0] - current_joints[0]) > 0.01, "robot didn't move"
232	                assert abs(paused_joints[0] - target_joints[0]) > 0.5, "motion wasn't paused early"
233	
234	                # The pause holds: execute() must still be pending.
235	                await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
236	                assert not motion_task.done(), "execute() returned on a resumable IO pause"
237	
238	                await kuka.write("OUT#900", False)
239	                await asyncio.wait_for(motion_task, timeout=60.0)
240	
241	                final_joints = await mg.joints()
242	                assert abs(final_joints[0] - target_joints[0]) < 0.01
243	            finally:
244	                await kuka.write("OUT#900", False)
245	                if not motion_task.done():
246	                    motion_task.cancel()
